summary.intent: Execute Phase 60 (IPNS Verification Cross-Layer Closeout) using wave-based parallel execution across 8 plans in 4 waves, hardening IPNS record verification to be strictly fail-closed across Rust and TypeScript layers.
summary.outcome: Wave 1 (plans 60-01, 60-02, 60-03) completed successfully with all 251 sdk-core tests passing. Wave 2 began with plan 60-04 dispatched but not yet returned in the transcript.

repo: Phase 60 has 8 plans across 4 waves; Wave 4 (60-08) is non-autonomous (staging wipe + redeploy + smoke-test) and requires a human-action checkpoint.
IPNS verify logic was split across crates: fuse/src/verify.rs had the canonical impl but sdk/fuse/desktop needed to share one impl via api-client/src/ipns.rs.
All 9 first-publish IPNS producers (FUSE, desktop Tauri, sdk-core, web) were using seq=0 instead of seq=1; the strict resolver requires seq=1 as a precondition.
VerifyError::Legacy variant was removed as part of D-04; all 9 FUSE caller arms were folded to use Invalid instead.
Windows winfsp site is CI-gated and not testable locally — expected gap in local test coverage.
vendored `fuser` crate has pre-existing dead-code warnings that appear in cargo check output but are not regressions.
crates/fuse/src/verify.rs was a re-export shim to be deleted after 60-04 re-points all imports.

code.finding: Was referencing VerifyError::Legacy which was removed in 60-01; executor folded to Invalid as part of compile necessity, not Wave 2 scope.
Had stale expectation of seq=0n that needed updating to 1n after 60-02 unified first-publish producers to seq=1.

workflow: Sequential gsd-executor subagents on the main working tree were chosen over worktree isolation because the worktree merge-back path is unreliable for a strict fail-closed crypto-cutover phase — correctness over wall-clock.

Executor agent mid-edit diagnostic snapshots can report stale compile errors (e.g. E0599 on VerifyError::Legacy) that are already resolved by the time the agent finishes; always re-run cargo check authoritatively before flagging as a failure.
Wave-level build/test gates (cargo check + full unit tests) are run after each wave completes to catch cross-plan integration issues before proceeding.

When a plan's compile necessity forces it to absorb work from a later plan's declared scope (60-01 folding FUSE Legacy arms instead of 60-04), the later plan's scope must be re-evaluated to avoid duplicating work.

friction: Worktree isolation mode (isolation='worktree') is not reliably supported for merge-back in this harness, forcing fallback to sequential main-tree execution and losing parallelism benefits.
Executor agent reported a stale E0599 compile error mid-edit that required a manual cargo check to disprove, adding diagnostic overhead.
60-01 was forced to fold 9 FUSE caller arms (originally 60-04's scope) as a compile necessity, creating scope bleed between waves that requires careful accounting.
Agent executor skills payload was empty — no project-specific executor skills registered, so executor prompts had no project-tailored guidance.
